newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle bid $62, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Friday at $62.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $63.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.
Sales were light to moderate on Thursday at $62.00, unchanged from the start of the week, but up $0.50 to $1.00 from the week's low on Wednesday.
Prices Thursday rallied amid steep advances in Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures and sold out showlists in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, they said.
"The key to our higher sales on Thursday was the big volume in Texas," one Kansas feedlot source said.

Packers had to raise bids to buy cattle remaining on showlists, the sources said. Week-to-date sales early Friday in the Panhandle area were pegged near 120,000 head, well above showlist estimates of 103,000. The Kansas weekly sales estimate Friday was near 89,000 head, slightly below the showlist estimate of 91,000 cattle feeders there said.
Fed cattle prices also were underpinned by strong beef movement this week after packers discounted boxed beef cut-out values, they said.
Sales were seen light Friday as owners wait until Monday in anticipation of higher prices, sources said.
